_comment: Guided tour for Plot Settings (emtk app). 'name' is the control: a field's attr, a button's action, '<section>.fold' for a section header, 'preview_plot' for the sample plot. Steps with an 'await' wait for the user to use the control.

steps.title: Change it on top, watch it below
steps.text:
Every edit in the sections above shows at once on the preview below: three sample curves (data, model, instrument response) drawn with the colours, line width, grid and legend you choose. They preview the styling and are not your data.

Settings are grouped into folding sections: backend, colours, appearance, node graphs and a pyqtgraph-only section.

steps.title: The backend is the how, not the what
steps.text: The rendering backend decides which engine draws a plot; the curves, ranges and selections stay as they are. A changed backend reaches plots that are created afterwards.

await.hint: Open the list and pick a backend.

steps.title: Pick a colour and watch the preview
steps.text: Click the swatch beside Data curve to open a colour picker, or type a hex value such as #22cc44 and press Enter. The preview curve changes at once, and the status line says the edit is not applied yet.

steps.title: Apply uses it, Save keeps it
steps.text: Apply writes the edits into the active settings: curves drawn from now on take the new colours, a fit already on screen keeps its colours until it is re-plotted. Save also writes them to the settings file for the next start; Reset reloads everything from the active settings and drops edits you did not apply.

steps.title: Appearance: line width, grid, legend
steps.text: Line width, font size, grid opacity and which furniture the plots show. The grid and legend options change the preview too.

steps.title: The folded section is engine-specific
steps.text: The advanced section holds the options that only exist on the pyqtgraph engine: anti-aliasing, panning and the background and foreground colours. They are inert under the native emtk backend, which is why they live in their own folded section. The preview follows the background.
